papers.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Chaotic Three-Body Dynamics in Astrophysics
papers.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Sim2Science: ML with Imperfect Scientific Models
papers.excerpt: Machine learning (ML) and generative AI have recently made impressive progress in understanding physics.
papers.tldr: A hierarchy of prediction problems stemming from chaotic three-body systems is explored and a range of ML approaches are benchmarked, including general-purpose prediction algorithms and those that build on top of foundational physics models.

papers.title: The PAU Survey: Self-supervised image denoising for flux-preserving photometry
papers.topic: Source Detection, Deblending and Image Simulation
papers.tldr: This work evaluates and improves Noise2Void for denoising real astronomical images, focusing on preserving fluxes, reducing photometric scatter, and retaining the main source features across a wide magnitude range, and shows that standard N2V systematically underestimates galaxy fluxes, especially for faint galaxies.

papers.title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
papers.excerpt: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics.
papers.tldr: These solvers enable scalable EoS inference that self-consistently accounts for rotation and repeated stellar-structure calculations during binary evolution, making spin predictions that account for rotational structure and EoS uncertainties computationally accessible to population synthesis.

papers.title: Spectroscopy-informed Deep Learning Searches for Photometric Little Red Dots in JWST Surveys
papers.comment: 11 figures (9 in the main text and 2 additional in appendix), 5 tables, to appear in ApJS soon 35 new LRD candidates with NIRSpec/PRISM are identified
papers.excerpt: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a population of compact, red sources discovered at high redshift with JWST that exhibit distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs).
papers.tldr: A cross-modal machine-learning framework is developed that combines matched NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy to transfer spectroscopic information into imaging-based representations, enabling LRD identification from JWST/NIRCam imaging alone.

papers.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): Selection of active galactic nuclei and star-formation emission with machine-learning techniques
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 19 pages, 20 figures, and two tables
papers.excerpt: Sources detected by recent large-area radio surveys require robust classification and characterisation.
papers.tldr: The ML-based pipeline provides a scalable way to produce large catalogues for the ongoing EMU survey and future Square Kilometre Array observations and reveals that multi-wavelength analysis can uncover radio populations and trends often missed by colour cuts or spectroscopy alone.

papers.title: Object-independent evaluation of small-data astronomical image classifiers: architecture, representation, and acquisition shortcuts
papers.excerpt: Reported performance in small astronomical image datasets can reflect object reuse, field-of-view differences, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived properties as well as astronomical morphology.
papers.tldr: These results demonstrate generalisation to unseen physical objects, but also show that image context, acquisition settings, and catalogue-derived object properties carry substantial class information.
